Legenda (publicada em inglês)

CEO out. Record quarter. 5 days apart. 

Nov 12: Jensen Huang stepped down and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. $NVDA fell 4.3% that day.
Nov 17: her first earnings. Revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y) vs ~$108.9B expected, and a $130B guide for next quarter.

The lesson: key-person risk is not the same as business risk. The numbers held. The open question is who leads next, and that's what to watch.

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

The Fed is about to hike. Again. 

September brought the first rate hike since 2023. October's CPI came in hot (+0.4% m/m, core +0.3% vs 0.2% expected). Now markets price roughly 9-in-10 odds of another hike on Dec 9.

Why your stocks care: higher rates shrink what future profits are worth today. $100 ten years out is worth ~$74 at 3%, but only ~$61 at 5%. The further out the profits, the bigger the hit.

The biggest IPO in history. Here's the receipt.

Publicado
DataQui 19 nov 2026 · 17h15 Lisboa · 12h15 Nova Iorque
FormatoReel
ÁreaMarkets
Instagramhttps://www.instagram.com/reel/Df7mEkdD6wy/

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

The biggest IPO in history. Here's the receipt.

Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) priced at $83, above its $70–78 range, raising ~$81.3B at a ~$1.5T valuation. It opened at $111.50 (+34% vs $83) at about 11:50 a.m. ET, a market value near $2T.

The numbers behind the headline:
• H1 revenue: $1.16B to $16.3B (~14x)
• Price-to-sales: ~46x annualized revenue
• H1 net loss: $80.7B, but ~$72.4B is a non-cash revaluation. Operating loss: $693M.
• P/E: officially none (it lost money). Using its best quarter (Q2 operating profit $974M × 4), $83 a share is ~385x profits. The S&P 500 trades near 18x.

In plain English: at today's profits, it would take ~385 years to earn back the $83 price. To look like a normal stock, profits would need to grow 20x+.

Updated to the $111.50 open: ~62x sales and ~517x best-quarter profits. Profits would need to grow ~29x.

Day one is the headline. The numbers are the story.

Your call: is $111.50 a share too much? What is Anthropic really worth? Tell us in the comments.

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

Trump, Xi and Putin in one room. A first. Here's what your portfolio should actually watch.

Today in Shenzhen, on the APEC sidelines, the three leaders held their first-ever three-way meeting. On the table, per US officials: trade, chips, rare earths, nuclear arms and the Iran war.

4 channels from summit to stocks:
1. Tariffs: new US-China lists cut tariffs on ~$30B of goods each way.
2. Rare earths: China's control pause runs to Jan 10, 2027.
3. Chip exports: Nvidia's next-quarter guide already assumes zero China data-center sales.
4. Oil: sanctions and the Iran war feed inflation, then the Fed.

Update: the leaders issued a 4-point declaration on nuclear stability, but no major breakthroughs.

Watch the paper, not the photo.

AMD, a short seller and a falling knife

Publicado
DataSex 20 nov 2026 · 03h Lisboa · 22h Nova Iorque (19 nov)
FormatoReel
ÁreaMarkets
Instagramhttps://www.instagram.com/reel/Df8pKVmArve/

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

AMD fell as much as ~9% in one morning. The trigger: a short seller.

Hunterbrook, which disclosed a bet against the stock, published a report alleging that a Chinese server maker on the US Entity List since 2025 kept shipping updates with newer AMD firmware.

AMD denies it, saying the claims misrepresent its business and that it complies with US export law. The report itself does not claim proof of a violation.

By the close: AMD down ~7.7%, Nasdaq down ~2%.

The lesson: a short report is a claim, not a verdict. Watch for the company's answer, and for regulators.

Your call: buying the dip, or catching a falling knife? Comment DIP or KNIFE

Yesterday (Thursday, Nov 19), Wall Street had a brutal day, and AI was at the center of it. 

The Dow lost 1,101 points (-2.2%) and closed below 50,000 for the first time since June. The S&P 500 fell 2%, its 6th straight loss, now 8.2% below its record. The tech-heavy Nasdaq, home of the AI giants, fell the most: -2.3%.

The AI dominoes:
1. AI leadership: Nvidia's CEO exit and a short-seller report on AMD (allegations AMD denies).
2. The AI IPO test: Anthropic opened +34%, closed +17% ($97.17). It couldn't revive confidence in AI.
3. Rates: markets expect another Fed hike on Dec 9, and higher rates hit the priciest growth stocks first.

Perspective: since 1980, the S&P 500 has dropped ~14% at some point in an average year, and still finished higher in roughly 3 of 4 years. -8% hurts. It's not unusual.

So, is the AI bubble popping? Today's open is minutes away.

Taiwan's stock market just had its worst week since 1991. 

While America slept, Thursday's AI selloff hit Asia, and it hit harder:
• Taiwan (Taiex): -6.2% today, -17.5% this week
• South Korea (Kospi): -5.2%. Samsung -6.9%, SK Hynix -6.1%
• Japan (Nikkei 225): -5.1%

Why Taiwan? It's the world's AI chip factory. TSMC alone is about 40% of the index, and it makes the chips for Nvidia, AMD and Apple. When investors doubt AI, Taiwan feels it first.

This morning we asked: red or green? The answer: red. The S&P 500 fell for a 7th straight day, its longest losing streak since 2020, and slid into a correction, more than 10% below its record.

For long-term investors, one bad week is not the story. The real question: can AI profits grow into these prices?

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

Nvidia now trades cheaper than the S&P 500 (on P/E). Its earnings just grew 111%. 

Is Nvidia stock cheap now, or a value trap? Swipe for both sides 

Friday: -14% to $125.53, its worst day since January 2025, after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining Nvidia's accounting (no charges; the SEC declined to comment). That's ~-48% from the Oct 6 record, ~$2.7 trillion of market cap gone, and 7 straight losing weeks.

The print didn't break:
• Q3 FY27 revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y), data center $107.6B
• Non-GAAP EPS $2.68 (+111% y/y) vs. $2.47 consensus
• Q4 guide $130B ±3%, assuming $0 China data-center compute

The multiple did. Annualize Q3 EPS ($10.72) and Nvidia trades at ~11.7x, below the S&P 500's ~17x forward P/E. Implied PEG ~0.11. Earnings yield ~8.5%.

The bull case: hypergrowth at a value multiple.
The bear case: a low P/E on peak earnings is the classic semis trap. And if regulators question the E, the P/E means nothing. Add a ~340 bps margin step-down, capex funded by thinning free cash flow and no permanent CEO.

The debate isn't the P. It's the durability (and credibility) of the E.

Your call: is Nvidia cheap, or a value trap? Comment CHEAP or TRAP

The fear gauge: VIX at its highest since April 2025

Publicado
DataDom 22 nov 2026 · 18h Lisboa · 13h Nova Iorque (+ Story 18h05)
FormatoReel
ÁreaInvestor psychology
Instagramhttps://www.instagram.com/reel/DgDaOh5oUiU/

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

Wall Street's fear gauge just hit its highest close since April 2025. 

On Friday, the VIX closed at 35.89, after touching 40 during the day.

What is the VIX? Think of it as the price of crash insurance: the market's expected S&P 500 swings over the next 30 days, priced from options. When investors panic, they pay up to protect their portfolios, and the VIX jumps.

How to read it:
• Below 20: calm
• Above 30: fear
• Above 40: panic

The twist: since 1998, when the VIX crossed 35, the S&P 500 was up about 28% a year later, on average (RBC; Cboe finds ~28% since 1990).

Not every time. In 2008, fear spiked and stocks kept falling for months. Averages are not guarantees.

But fear is usually loudest near the bottom, not the top. That's when panic selling does the most damage to long-term investors.

Your call: is this fear a warning, or an opportunity? Comment WARNING or OPPORTUNITY

Bonds at ~5%: why own stocks? (earnings yield vs Treasuries)

Pronto, à espera de aprovação
DataTer 24 nov 2026 · —
FormatoReel
ÁreaTimeless lesson
Instagram—

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

A 10-year US Treasury now pays almost 5%, backed by the US government. So why take the risk of owning stocks? 

Here's the math. Flip the P/E and you get the earnings yield: the profit you buy with every $100.

• S&P 500: ~17.5x next year's profits → earnings yield ~5.7%
• 10-year Treasury: ~4.9%
• The extra pay for owning stocks: less than 1 point. That's thin.

But a bond's payment is fixed. Company profits can grow. That's the long-term edge.

Since 1928, US stocks returned about 10% a year on average (dividends included). 10-year Treasuries: about 4.5% (Damodaran, NYU Stern).

Stocks pay more over time because they can hurt more along the way. Like last week's -8.6%.

Your call: at ~5%, are bonds the smarter buy for the next 10 years, or do stocks still win? Comment BONDS or STOCKS

October PCE came in HOT + Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%

Pronto, à espera de aprovação
DataQua 25 nov 2026 · —
FormatoCarrossel
ÁreaFed, rates and US macro
Instagram—

Legenda (publicada em inglês)

HOT.  The Fed's favorite inflation gauge came in above forecasts.

October PCE (released today):
• Core PCE: 3.3% year over year vs. 3.2% expected (+0.3% on the month)
• Headline PCE: 3.8%, in line with forecasts (+0.3% on the month)

PCE in plain English: how much prices rose on everything Americans spend money on. Core strips out food and energy to show the trend underneath. The Fed's target is 2%, and inflation is moving away from it.

The other big number: Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualized (from 3.4%; ~3.5% expected). Consumer spending: 4.2%.

Strong growth + sticky inflation = little reason for the Fed to ease up. A December 9 hike was already priced in; now it looks locked in.

The long-term lens: one month is one data point. Over decades, company earnings have tended to keep up with inflation better than fixed payments. Rates move valuations now; your plan runs 10+ years.

Your call: on Dec 9, does the Fed hike by 0.25, or go bigger? Comment QUARTER or BIGGER
